prompt:
A jet aircraft lands on an aircraft carrier flight deck. The aircraft touches down with a horizontal speed of 65.0 m s^-1. An arresting wire engages the tailhook of the aircraft, bringing it to rest with uniform deceleration.
(a) If the aircraft travels a distance of 78.0 m along the flight deck before coming to rest, calculate the time taken for the aircraft to stop. [2 marks]
(b) Calculate the acceleration of the aircraft during this braking period. [2 marks]
(c) In an emergency where the arresting cable snaps immediately after touchdown, the pilot applies maximum wheel braking, which provides a deceleration of only 4.20 m s^-2. Calculate the minimum runway length required to stop the aircraft from 65.0 m s^-1, and state with a reason whether an aircraft carrier deck of length 250 m is sufficient. [2 marks]

response_structure.description: Calculation of stopping time during cable arrest.
Calculation of acceleration during cable arrest with sign.
Calculation of stopping distance under emergency braking and deck comparison.

hints: Use s = 0.5 (u + v) t with u = 65.0 m s^-1, v = 0, and s = 78.0 m.
Rearrange to solve for stopping time t.
Use v = u + at or v^2 = u^2 + 2as.
Pay attention to the negative sign indicating deceleration.
walkthrough: Step 1: Apply v = u + at => 0 = 65.0 + a(2.40).
common_pitfalls: Omitting the negative sign when asked for acceleration.

hints: Use v^2 = u^2 + 2as with a = -4.20 m s^-2 and v = 0.
Compare the calculated distance to 250 m.
walkthrough: Step 3: Compare: 503 m > 250 m, so the deck is not sufficient (aircraft will overrun).
common_pitfalls: Stating the deck is sufficient based on time rather than distance.

hints: Break the scenario into the two different braking conditions: cable arrest vs wheel braking.
Always state whether acceleration is directed opposite to velocity.
solution:
(a) s = 0.5(u + v)t => 78.0 = 0.5(65.0 + 0)t => t = 78.0 / 32.5 = 2.40 s.
(b) a = (v - u) / t = (0 - 65.0) / 2.40 = -27.1 m s^-2 (deceleration of 27.1 m s^-2).
(c) v^2 = u^2 + 2as => 0 = 65.0^2 + 2(-4.20)s => s = 4225 / 8.40 = 503 m. The 250 m deck is not sufficient because 503 m > 250 m (the aircraft would run off the end of the deck).
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: In part (a), use s = 0.5(u + v)t: 78.0 = 0.5(65.0)t => t = 2.40 s [2 marks].
Step 2: In part (b), use v = u + at: 0 = 65.0 + a(2.40) => a = -27.1 m s^-2 [2 marks].
Step 3: In part (c), calculate emergency stopping distance: s = u^2 / (2a) = 4225 / 8.40 = 503 m [1 mark].
Step 4: Conclude clearly that 503 m exceeds the 250 m deck length, so it is insufficient [1 mark].
